candidates.name: Factitious disorder
support_spans: Clues suggesting volitional behavior included selective acceptance of benzodiazepines and gabapentin while refusing other medications, eating all meals despite “stupor,” abruptly lapsing into and out of catatonia-like and psychotic behaviors depending on the topic of conversation, purposeful movements to obtain lorazepam after seizures, and evidence of self‐induced urinary incontinence during one episode.
candidates.why: The patient's behavior and symptoms suggest a pattern of factitious disorder, where she is intentionally producing or feigning symptoms for attention or other gains.

candidates.name: Conversion disorder
support_spans: catatonia-like signs: flat affect with psychomotor retardation and fluctuating mutism
seizure-like behavior: episodes of head jerking with eye fluttering without tongue biting
contradict_spans: A regional catatonia specialist evaluated her and noted that she was unlikely to have catatonia
